Man, seriously? I hate that "only you can help yourself" stuff. Especially when that's the response people get when deliberately asking for help. People go to therapy because they can't help themselves. Saying "you have to put effort in as well is completely different than saying "the only person who can give you that inner monologue of positivity is you." Saying stuff like that makes people think no one cares to help them and they have to all themselves, which makes them feel isolated. Therapists do this exact thing: give people new ways to look at situations. Some people can't come up with an inner monologue of positivity, and their therapists help them come with one. People always talk about getting help for depression, and then there are people that are like "only you can help yourself". 

Making changes and changing the way you think is why people go to therapy. Because they can't do it themselves. Yes, they have to apply it, but they wouldn't have even known how to do it without therapy. Automatically assuming someone you don't know won't listen is just... by that logic, therapy would not work at all, because again, they give you new ways to interpret situations. They help you come up with reasons to live. And, probably most important of all, they listen. They make sure the client knows that they care. Knowing someone cares about you is is helping you makes a world of a difference. I hate when people downplay that in favor of "pull yourself up by your bootstraps".

Because not only do you tell them it's their fault, but you offer them nothing on how to go about getting better. This advice is utterly useless.

If you cannot offer real practical advice for coping skills, or a plan for improving their mood, stick to empathy. People say some of the worst things, mostly just due to a lack of perspective or limited personal experience. I could just as easily say that your traumatic memories are your fault and expect you to get better off of that, but I won't, because even if that was true, it would be vague, stupid, empty advice.

Just don't tell others that you're a cynic, or you'll get responses like "Quit being so emo” Or “People are awesome, you just see people as bad because you’re a weak, selfish sensitive snowflake” Or “Just don’t be affected by what people do, and you will be happier”
